title: Validated numerical polynomial roots
objective: Implement a bounded ordinary-Python numerical polynomial-root solver with complex roots, scale-safe validation, adversarial differential corpora, documentation, and benchmark evidence
references: Bini and Fiorentino, Design, analysis, and implementation of a multiprecision polynomial rootfinder

handoff.summary: Adds a bounded degree-64 binary64 polynomial-root vertical slice with inspectable planning, Aberth--Ehrlich iteration, bounded Laguerre rescue, finite JSON, semantic traces, cancellation and resource budgets, logarithmic scaling, independent term-wise backward validation, Vieta reconstruction, condition estimates, honest numerical clusters, CPython and Sage.js integration tests, NumPy/mpmath differential oracles, algorithm survey documentation, and representative performance evidence.
risks: This is the correct ordinary-Python fallback, not an industrial accelerator: the recorded degree-64 Linux x64 workload is about one second and roughly 450 times slower than the NumPy companion baseline.
Multiplicity is never certified; catastrophically conditioned clusters may use a shared numerical representative only when both backward residuals and complete Vieta reconstruction improve.
Only local Linux x64 CPython and Sage.js Python-mode receipts exist. Browser, SEA, Linux ARM64, macOS ARM64, and Windows x64 support remains explicitly pending qualification.

The inherited integration workspace currently fails architecture:check and merge:check before reaching this module because src/lib/sagejs/numerics/approximation/__init__.py has no package owner; this lane did not edit the shared package graph.
next_steps: Integration must export the public symbols from src/lib/sagejs/numerics/approximation/__init__.py and add polynomial_roots.py to the centrally owned strict-Python and package-graph surfaces.
Integration must include the focused test directory in the central numerical test/discovery surface and rerun architecture:check after repairing the inherited approximation package owner.
Qualify browser, SEA, Linux ARM64, macOS ARM64, and Windows x64 before changing the capability record's pending platform claims.
Evaluate a qualified MPSolve or LAPACK-class backend later against the same corpus; retain this implementation as the dynamic fallback and independent post-validator.
